mode: scenario-adaptation; full upstream test snapshot retained separately for audit, not executed as Ker coverage; no upstream network implementation copied

native-udp-functional-matrix.adaptation: Batch Linux-specific UDP functional validation, not additional migrated upstream test cases. Identical host/native IPv4/IPv6 public-API contract matrix; independent-host IPv6 client/server ancillary/error-queue/fragmentation/software-segmentation/ASM/SSM tests; IPv4 SSM third-source rejection and limited broadcast; actual independent-router IPv4/IPv6 PMTU1280 errors/cache/local rejection/recovery; raw independent checksum/reverse-fragment/reassembly-expiry/reorder/duplicate vectors. Require complete wire IPv6 fragment reassembly/checksums, native per-family UDP/reassembly counters and zero outstanding worker buffers. The host-signal interruption probe confirms an unsupported boundary and never counts as a functional pass. Machine report binds actual CTest outcomes, rejects omitted/skipped/missing cases and preserves physical-NIC/endurance/extended-runtime gaps. Original Linux owns all protocol behavior. No upstream edits or F-Stack API/full-fixture equivalence claim.

native-fstack-ipv6-route.adaptation: Related gateway feature evidence only; the catalog source case remains blocked because it asserts INET6-disabled ignore semantics, and the IPv6 VIP and VLAN feature evidence is recorded separately, without full fixture equivalence. Add explicit Linux [network] gateway6/--gateway6, require address6, support global and link-local next hops through a Ker rtnetlink request to the original Linux main route table with RTA_OIF, and honor original Linux gateway checks without ONLINK. Validate CLI/INI syntax and precedence before setup, remove inherited internal gateway overrides, fail125 on invalid off-link next hop before application readiness and clean up worker. Actual DPDK net_tap connects the native private kernel to an independent Linux router and a third remote Linux namespace across two /64 subnets. Test INI global gateway and CLI replacement by link-local gateway, TCP/UDP both directions, exact bytes and explicit native source addresses, UDP send hop limit64/receive63 at both endpoints, router Ip6OutForwDatagrams increase, native TCP counters and zero outstanding buffers. Omission with a conflicting ambient override must leave TCP/UDP off-subnet connect returning ENETUNREACH. No dynamic routing/failover, RA/SLAAC, physical NIC or complete FreeBSD fixture equivalence claim; upstream sources remain unchanged.

native-fstack-network-sysctl.adaptation: Partial adaptation only: Ker [sysctl] and repeatable --sysctl accept explicit Linux net.* names, merge CLI by key, bound entries/key/value sizes, reject malformed paths and conflicting tcp_ecn options before setup. Production constructor writes private original Linux procfs before native READY; Linux validates values, unknown keys and invalid values fail125 before main. Actual DPDK net_tap startup tests five socket defaults (IP_TTL, TCP_KEEPIDLE, TCP_KEEPINTVL, TCP_KEEPCNT, TCP_SYNCNT), CLI replacement retaining the other four, omission preserving pinned Linux defaults despite inherited KER_NATIVE_SYSCTLS, and unknown-key/invalid-value failure cleanup. Host namespace sysctl files remain unchanged; require actual successful EAL cleanup and zero outstanding buffers. The upstream fixture combines boot and five sysctl entries; this covers multiple effective Linux network settings, not its FreeBSD names, boot hz/physmem/fd_reserve/mem_size/panicstr or internal list layout. No upstream or protocol implementation changes.

native-fstack-ipv6-interop.adaptation: Related feature evidence only; the catalog source case remains blocked and is not counted as adapted/partial. The pinned valid_inet6.ini fixture supplies IPv6 addresses/prefixes, gateways, VIPs and VLAN configuration, but its registered test asserts INET6-disabled ignore semantics. Ker adds explicit Linux [network] address6/--address6 with syntax/precedence validation and inherited override removal, enables DPDK multicast reception for NDP, and uses unchanged original LKL lkl_if_add_ip and lkl_if_wait_ipv6_dad after interface-up, including original Linux DAD. Real net_tap tests inbound/outbound IPv6 TCP and UDP, explicit native source binds, unconfigured-address bind rejection, independent-host NDP resolving the worker MAC, IPv4 TCP alongside IPv6, native TCP counters and zero outstanding buffers. Two runs cover INI and CLI replacement; actual host-owned duplicate address fails125 before native READY/main and cleans up worker. This specific CTest does not claim FreeBSD INET6-disabled behavior, gateway, IPv6 VIP/VLAN, RA/SLAAC, cross-subnet or physical NIC coverage; gateway and VIP evidence have separate provenance entries. No upstream/protocol source modifications.

native-fstack-vip-addresses.adaptation: Ker [network] address and comma-separated vip_addresses, or repeatable --vip-address CLI options, install primary and additional IPv4 addresses through unchanged original LKL lkl_if_set_ipv4 (RTM_NEWADDR CREATE|EXCL). CLI entries replace the INI list; omitted entries install none. Validate typed addresses, prefixes, duplicate primary/VIPs, empty lists and a32-entry limit before library/worker resolution. Real DPDK net_tap and original Linux in two runs (INI and CLI override) expose exactly the primary198.18.0.2/24 plusVIPs198.18.0.3/24 and198.18.0.4/24. The app checks actual SIOCGIFCONF addresses, UP flags and masks; an unconfigured198.18.0.99 bind must fail EADDRNOTAVAIL despite conflicting ambient/overridden values. Independent host TCP connects to all3 addresses; explicit VIP source binds make2 outbound connections whose host-observed peers match. Original native TCP counters and zero outstanding worker buffers are required. This adapts address/VIP configuration scenarios, not F-Stack port_cfgs layout, FreeBSD APIs, VLAN VIPs, failover or VRRP. Protocol/ARP behavior remains original Linux; no upstream changes.

native-fstack-startup-failures.adaptation: Run the actual Ker launcher, production preload/guard plus a separate test-only preload variant and original DPDK net_tap worker in a private network namespace. A successful control must execute the interface probe and publish native statistics. Test-only host CLOCK_REALTIME EIO is restricted to the application preload by its startup/packet environment: original Linux boots, then the production realtime adapter fails before native READY and main. A real off-subnet gateway is rejected by original Linux during network bring-up. A separate non-installed library compiles the exact same Ker adaptation sources and pinned liblkl with link-time wrappers for lkl_init, lkl_netdev_add, lkl_start_kernel and lkl_if_up; no hook exists in the production library. Its successful control forwards to real LKL initialization, device registration, kernel boot, loopback and device activation. Inject EIO separately at init, registration and boot; an exact stage trace must stop at the failed boundary, with successful real prerequisite stages and no later calls. Variadic kernel command-line arguments are formatted and forwarded to the real boot function in the control. Injected loopback EIO must stop before device activation; injected device EIO follows successful real loopback activation and must reach the production interface-activation failure handler. Exact host-side traces prove these stages; neither failure may send native READY or execute main. These are injected adapter-return failures, not organic internal kernel/NIC faults or full F-Stack stage equivalence. Unknown ethdev lookup fails in the worker before native startup; retain its already-consumed DONE snapshot in launcher --stats. Every case requires actual successful rte_eal_cleanup and zero outstanding mbufs; failures return125 and leave no application marker/native success statistics. Monotonic host clocks and upstream sources are unchanged. No FreeBSD initialization ABI or exit1 equivalence is claimed.

native-fstack-packet-device.adaptation: Link production packet-device.c and invoke its actual lkl_dev_net_ops callbacks over nonblocking AF_UNIX datagrams and a real eventfd. Verify context allocation/ops/vnet-header capability, exact free counts and descriptor balance across repeated lifetimes. A test-only calloc wrapper injects ENOMEM but forwards all successful allocations and every free to libc; actual RLIMIT_NOFILE exhaustion makes eventfd fail with EMFILE, preserving caller fd ownership. Additional Ker adapter checks exercise byte-exact scatter/gather TX/RX, empty RX and TX backpressure readiness, oversize RX truncation rejection/consumption, invalid vector counts, interrupted ppoll retry and repeated stop. Observe the polling thread in actual SYS_ppoll via /proc before signaling and stopping; join before freeing, require ESHUTDOWN/HUP afterward and close both owned fds while preserving the peer. This adapts only F-Stack context construction/destruction scenarios, not FreeBSD softc/ifp, lkl_netdev_add/remove registration or protocol behavior. Upstream source is unchanged; null-context mbuf ownership remains unsupported and uncounted.

native-fstack-worker-clock.adaptation: Use the production DPDK worker monotonic-nanosecond adapter. Unwrapped host CLOCK_MONOTONIC samples are positive and advance across a real sleep. Test-only wrapping additionally checks exact seconds/nanoseconds conversion, INT64_MAX bounds, invalid samples, EIO, unchanged output on failure and recovery. A real net_tap worker in a private namespace drains successfully with the host clock, then a second worker receives one injected CLOCK_MONOTONIC EIO after READY and before control-channel drain. It must report nonzero status with a clock diagnostic, emit exactly one DONE with zero outstanding mbufs and call actual rte_eal_cleanup successfully. This adapts the upstream positive/non-regressing nanosecond scenario; no CPU TSC/frequency conversion or ff_get_tsc_ns ABI equivalence is claimed. Kernel protocol clocks and upstream implementations are unchanged.

native-fstack-entropy.adaptation: Seed original Linux RNG from32 actual host SYS_getrandom syscall (flags0) bytes after private kernel boot and before application sockets are exposed. Original Linux RNDADDENTROPY mixes the seed and credits256 bits, followed by RNDRESEEDCRNG to rekey immediately even when already initialized; a private rootfs random-device node is unlinked immediately after open, descriptors close, and seed storage is explicitly wiped on every return. Actual original-kernel getrandom(GRND_NONBLOCK) fills64 bytes with the pinned >=50 nonzero threshold and yields >=12 changes across16 words. A test-only syscall wrapper injects EIO/zero/EINTR, failure after a real short read, and caps real successful reads at7 bytes; a deterministic getrandom symbol shim confirms seeding bypasses interposition, while successful entropy always comes from the real host RNG, never test constants. Both retry and ordinary/reseed paths use real original Linux ioctl/getrandom; host seeding invokes SYS_getrandom directly. A real private-path collision propagates EEXIST and preserves marker contents. This is a Linux RNG scenario adaptation, not FreeBSD arc4random API or algorithm equivalence; output sanity tests are not a cryptographic-strength proof. No custom PRNG, deterministic fallback, GRND_INSECURE, upstream modification or host random-device write.

native-fstack-realtime.adaptation: Boot original Linux and invoke the same private realtime synchronization adapter used by the production constructor. Reset only native realtime to an obsolete2000 epoch, synchronize from real host CLOCK_REALTIME, and require native seconds/nanoseconds to lie within host bracketing reads and exceed the pinned2020 threshold. Native realtime advances after a real sleep; native monotonic advancement tracks host monotonic across the epoch change. Test-only clock_gettime wrapping forwards all monotonic reads to the real host clock. Host realtime EIO propagates without setting native time; a successful host read with invalid nanoseconds reaches original Linux clock_settime and returns EINVAL without mutating the old epoch. Recovery and repeated synchronization succeed. No host clock is set, upstream kernel code changed, or FreeBSD cached-time/NULL-output API equivalence claimed.

native-fstack-lcore-mask.adaptation: Ker --lcore-mask / [dpdk] lcore_mask accepts nonzero hex with optional0x/0X and surrounding whitespace, preserves multi-bit selection, and rejects blank/zero/non-hex before library or worker setup. CLI overrides INI before mask validation. Competing EAL -c/-l/--lcores selections are rejected rather than silently rewritten; original DPDK validates CPU availability and hardware/build limits. Real net_tap TCP in both roles uses two allowed physical CPUs in the INI mask, then CLI override to one of them. Actual DPDK lcore_count/main_lcore and host sched_getcpu are checked, plus original Linux TCP open counters, bidirectional Ethernet traffic and zero outstanding buffers. This adapts parsing/core-selection scenarios; F-Stack nb_procs/proc_lcore memory layout, process-per-core behavior, process-id selection, secondary processes and OOM paths are not implemented or claimed. Existing raw EAL mapping works unchanged when mask is absent.

native-fstack-worker-traffic.adaptation: Actual ker-io-worker with original DPDK net_tap in a private user/network namespace, no mocked EAL or counters. Idle start followed by repeated real control-channel stop requests and EOF must emit exactly one successful DONE with zero packets/bytes/directional validation drops/retries/outstanding. A second real worker forwards three exact Ethernet frames of60/127/1514 bytes each direction between independent host AF_PACKET and the native packet channel; expected counts are3 packets/1701 bytes each way. Two malformed channel frame lengths increment only TX validation drops; aggregate dropped remains2. Channel framing and complete received bytes are checked. Both stops close the ethdev and report zero in-use mbufs. The test harness uses SIGSTOP/SIGCONT only as a scheduling barrier while it queues both control bytes and closes the pipe; worker shutdown is still driven by the real control channel and EOF. This adapts zero-init traffic and idempotent stop scenarios, without F-Stack ff_traffic_args/getter/stop ABI or Linux networking coverage claims. Byte counts exclude the12-byte channel header and FCS; TX counts PMD acceptance and RX counts successful channel delivery, once per frame rather than retry. Drops are adapter validation drops, not NIC hardware or shutdown-discard counters.

native-fstack-fd-map.adaptation: Real original Linux boot with actual Ker fd-table.c, no mocked native close. Establish, look up, replace and clear host-placeholder/native-socket mappings; verify real socket types, host close-on-exec flags, native descriptor release and host reservation release. Retained references preserve the replaced UDP object until put; a duplicated native TCP descriptor survives clearing its sibling. Host dup replacement clears the native association. Invalid lookups/closes are rejected safely; out-of-range fixed export reports EMFILE and consumes its native input. Ker uses NULL/errno and ownership-taking exports instead of F-Stack zero-sentinel/no-op setters; no FreeBSD offset encoding ABI claim.

native-fstack-errno.adaptation: All 81 symbolic errors in the pinned source table are checked using original LKL Linux UAPI inputs and host errno expectations, plus unknown error99999 passthrough. The production inline conversion shared by POSIX socket wrappers and fd-table close is tested directly: negative Linux returns become -1/host errno, while zero, positive and LONG_MAX successes preserve errno and value. Real original Linux boot additionally checks EBADF, EINVAL, EAFNOSUPPORT and ENOTCONN from actual syscalls and a successful socket/getpid/close sequence. Linux values share the host ABI; this adapts the error-translation scenario without accepting FreeBSD numeric errno inputs or changing upstream code.

native-fstack-tcp-ecn.adaptation: Typed Ker [network] tcp_ecn or --tcp-ecn accepts off/passive/on and CLI precedence, rejects unknown values before library resolution, and preserves the original Linux policy when omitted. Modes map to Linux sysctl0/2/1 respectively; F-Stack/FreeBSD tcp_ecn=1 means passive, so its intent maps to Ker passive/Linux2 rather than copying the integer. The explicit-enable scenario is adapted; default-off remains partial because native Linux defaults to2. Only private imported-kernel /proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_ecn is written, using original sysctl validation; startup fails on write errors. Real net_tap TCP runs eight mode/role combinations against an independently configured host peer, plus a host-reference handshake. Both peers check negotiated TCP_INFO ECN and payload. Native procfs diagnostics report the effective policy; counters and zero outstanding validate the original stack and cleanup. Actual SYN ECE/CWR and SYN-ACK ECE flags are checked from TX/RX captures. An inherited internal env override is removed so omission preserves Linux defaults. No F-Stack configuration-struct or sibling hz/mem_size ABI claim; no custom TCP implementation, CE-marked congestion response, external IPv6 or AccECN claim. ECN parser tests also require sibling address, port and parsed EAL tokens to remain unchanged.

native-fstack-mtu-config.adaptation: Actual Ker launcher parser accepts [network] mtu/max_mtu or --mtu/--max-mtu, defaults to1500/9000 and applies CLI precedence. Both are bounded1280..9000 and mtu must not exceed max_mtu. Reject actual9000 against an independently configured2000 ceiling, non-numeric max_mtu and out-of-range1279/9001/65535 with argparse status2 before resolving nonexistent libraries. Equal bounds1280/2000/9000 and overrides of either MTU or ceiling are tested. Real net_tap jumbo interop first rejects9000/2000 before launch, then overrides max_mtu to9000 and runs original Linux TCP/UDP in both roles, DF payload/EMSGSIZE checks, full9014-byte captures and zero outstanding. This single-port deployment ceiling is not hardware capability discovery. With live MTU support it also bounds runtime ioctl changes; large mode reserves frame capacity up to this ceiling so growth does not replace a live pool. Actual MTU still configures original Linux/DPDK. Ker mode=large keeps contiguous buffers, while mode=scatter uses standard-size segments with real 9000-byte TX/RX coverage in native-fstack-mbuf-scatter. These Ker runtime paths do not claim F-Stack mtu_enable/mbuf_mode or per-port array ABI equivalence; the F-Stack disabled-mtu-enable scenario remains blocked.

native-fstack-mtu-default.adaptation: Existing real startup probe checks original Linux interface MTU1500 and DPDK READY diagnostics MTU1500 when no new setting is supplied, plus real TCP and complete shutdown. F-Stack internal default flags are represented by Ker default behavior, fixed maximum9000 and contiguous packet buffers, not its config structs.

native-fstack-jumbo-mtu.adaptation: INI-provided MTU9000 configures actual DPDK port and original Linux interface. Real net_tap/veth links use9000; TCP transfers and UDP payloads0/1/1472/8972 run against independent host peers in both native roles plus host-reference UDP. IP_MTU must be9000; DF payload8973 fails with EMSGSIZE. Native UDP counters and zero fragmentation/reassembly plus PCAP in each direction require an actual complete9014-byte Ethernet frame containing an unfragmented9000-byte IPv4 UDP packet. Zero outstanding mbufs required. The Ker adapter negotiates original LKL virtio mergeable RX buffers for jumbo; checksum/segmentation offloads stay disabled. DPDK uses contiguous buffers sized with Ethernet/CRC/headroom. No modified upstream code, FreeBSD scatter API, DPDK scatter mode or external IPv6 jumbo claim.

native-fstack-empty-datagram-readiness.adaptation: The zero-data/no-EOF read-readiness scenario is exercised with actual zero-length UDP datagrams instead of synthetic FreeBSD kqueue events. Eighteen combinations cover IPv4/IPv6 loopback, LT/ET/ONESHOT and epoll_wait/epoll_pwait/epoll_pwait2. Require EPOLLIN with the full 64-bit event tag and no HUP/RDHUP/ERR while FIONREAD reports zero; MSG_PEEK preserves the empty datagram; LT repeats readiness, ET/ONESHOT do not repeat, and ONESHOT explicitly rearms the unread datagram. Normal recv consumes it, the next recv yields EAGAIN, and a later one-byte datagram delivers readiness and data. The same program runs on independent host Linux and through libker-posix/original Linux; output must match. Native IPv4 UDP counters require at least 18 sent/received datagrams and zero outstanding worker mbufs; IPv6 coverage is native loopback, not external IPv6 deployment. Separate existing native-fstack-udp-interop now explicitly rejects UDP HUP/RDHUP/ERR across independent IPv4 host peers including empty payloads; this extension is not an additional upstream case. No upstream source edits or protocol implementation.

native-fstack-host-failure.adaptation: Pinned F-Stack clock-error assertion and panic-abort scenarios adapted to Ker-installed lkl_host_ops.time/panic callbacks. Test-only linker wrapping fails only CLOCK_MONOTONIC with EIO in a forked child; valid clock calls forward to the real host clock, with nanosecond bounds, monotonicity and advancement checks. Both failed clock and panic must terminate with SIGABRT, not return. The same actual adapter and test are compiled with assertions enabled and with NDEBUG; checks do not use assert. No kernel boot failure or realtime-cache failure injection claim. Separate native-fstack-host-runtime installs this same clock adapter, then boots/halts original Linux with measured real time callbacks. No imported source modification or network protocol implementation.

native-fstack-startup-lifecycle-device.adaptation: Real net_tap EAL primary process and one available port; READY diagnostics query rte_eth_dev_socket_id and rte_eth_link_get_nowait. A socket in imported Linux queries SIOCGIFCONF/SIOCGIFFLAGS/SIOCGIFMTU, verifying loopback and configured IPv4 interface UP with MTU 1500. Launcher persists worker startup diagnostics and native/worker shutdown counters; active and passive TCP against independent host peers require TX/RX, native opens and zero outstanding mbufs. Traffic query is adapted to shutdown JSON rather than the F-Stack traffic struct/API; kernel protocol behavior comes from original Linux. No FreeBSD interface registration or hardware offload claim.

native-fstack-startup-lifecycle-init.adaptation: Actual Ker launcher starts real DPDK worker and imported Linux before application main; app marker and native interface ioctls prove startup, native DONE plus zero outstanding prove shutdown. Missing configuration exits 2; real EAL argument rejection and missing selected ethdev exit 125 without executing the application, instead of F-Stack exit(1). No mocked successful startup or FreeBSD boot failure; kernel/device/interface return-error injection is covered separately by native-fstack-startup-failures. Run/stop mapping remains partial: real worker control-channel stop and native teardown, without the ff_run callback/argument forwarding ABI.

native-fstack-launcher-config.adaptation: Eighteen pinned F-Stack INI scenarios adapted to the actual Ker launcher configuration reader: known sections/options, multiple sections, comments and whitespace, empty text/value, missing final newline, colon delimiter, valid UTF-8 BOM, malformed syntax, missing bracket, bare lines, real open-file/filename input, missing file and malformed BOM byte rejection. Python configparser exceptions and UTF-8 decode errors replace F-Stack integer return codes and callback records; typed Ker configuration, not direct F-Stack config-file/API compatibility. One multiline scenario remains partial because Ker joins lines into an EAL string instead of invoking a handler per line. No sectionless globals, arbitrary handler rejection/userdata, NULL FILE C ABI or section-name truncation claim; supported long sysctl-key retention is qualified separately. Ker extensions test strict unknown/default rejection and final-value duplicate-key precedence, interpolation disabled, CLI and negative-boolean overrides, config-relative paths, app argument isolation and pre-launch configuration rejection. Separate native-fstack-launcher-config-interop starts real DPDK/native Linux TCP workers in both roles using file-provided network/EAL/log/capture settings; validates kernel opens, TX/RX, zero outstanding, capture/log files and explicit CLI port/stats overrides. Its INI also repeats [sysctl] sections in A-B-A order for ip_unprivileged_port_start and ip_local_port_range; both native TCP roles prove the final surviving range-then-boundary order is accepted by original Linux.

native-fstack-worker-log.adaptation: Thirteen pinned F-Stack logging scenarios adapted to real, unwrapped DPDK log APIs and the actual worker log helper: file creation and append, invalid-directory failure, nonzero instance ID in filename, closing open/empty state, stream reset, global/type filtering, invalid-category error, variadic/literal/va_list formatting and actual DPDK byte-count returns. The unit test reads exact output and checks descriptor closure and a valid restored stderr stream. Ker uses one ker.io category and ker-io-<instance>.log instead of FreeBSD/library category pairs and F-Stack global configuration; runtime instance is the real worker PID. Mocked arbitrary rte_vlog returns are replaced with actual output counts and invalid-category errors. Ker additionally checks ferror because pinned DPDK ignores fflush errors, and reports existing stream errors and buffered-close failures with /dev/full. Separate native-fstack-worker-log-interop validates both original-Linux TCP roles over real DPDK, lifecycle log files and launcher status 125 on real worker log I/O errors. No FreeBSD logging API, application stderr redirection, rotation, or cross-process shared log sink is claimed.

native-fstack-thread-runtime.adaptation: Actual LKL host thread callbacks validate argument propagation and wrapper-allocation failure (test-only linker --wrap=malloc fails one allocation, with real thread callbacks and no successful thread stubs). LKL returns a zero thread handle on failure rather than -ff_ENOMEM. Basic creation and join-result cases remain partial: FreeBSD pcurthread inheritance and F-Stack discarded-return-value assertions have no equivalent LKL callback interface. Ker extensions verify four real concurrent host threads, self/equal identity, join completion, empty child TLS, distinct per-thread values, destructor execution, parent isolation, key reuse, semaphore gating and mutex counter integrity. A Ker pthread TLS adapter handles NULL allocation before dereference; injected allocation failure and real pthread-key exhaustion check errors and allocation cleanup. Original Linux boots and halts with measured real host-thread creation. No FreeBSD context emulation, application pthread interposition, cancellation, detached-thread lifetime or scheduler-equivalence claim. Ker mutex adapters now preserve real pthread synchronization while returning NULL with errno on allocation, attribute initialization/type, mutex initialization or attribute-destruction failure, with complete object/attribute unwind. Test-only per-thread linker wrappers inject each stage, count live allocations/attributes/mutexes, and verify real normal/recursive recovery after every failure. Four-thread mutual exclusion remains required, and original Linux boot must actually allocate adapted host mutexes. A pre-thread child verifies destroying a locked mutex aborts rather than freeing a live object; void lock/unlock/free callbacks fail explicitly on pthread errors. These mutexes protect original LKL virtual-CPU ownership across host threads and are not DPDK packet-loop locks; no lock-elision or single-owner scheduler claim is made. Ker now also owns pthread start-wrapper allocation: a pthread_create error frees that allocation, returns the LKL zero handle, and sets errno from the pthread error number. Per-test-thread EAGAIN/EPERM injection checks allocation balance, no failed callback invocation and errno conversion from a distinct sentinel. A subsequent real pthread create/join after each failure validates argument delivery and exactly one wrapper free before callback entry, including DEBUG/NDEBUG variants. Original Linux boot creates actual threads through the adapter with faults disabled. This does not qualify real host thread exhaustion, scheduling-policy configuration, pthread interposition for applications, or change FreeBSD context propagation limits. Additional real-thread lifecycle coverage exercises normal return and the actual host thread_exit callback with cleared TLS, finite three-pass destructor repopulation and repopulation beyond the host-advertised _SC_THREAD_DESTRUCTOR_ITERATIONS minimum. For requests above that minimum, callbacks run at least the advertised count and no more than the finite requested count. Each destructor must observe its TLS slot already cleared. Join must wait for all destructor passes; explicit thread_exit must not return. Parent TLS is not inherited and remains unchanged, and deleting a key with a parent value does not invoke its destructor. Default, DEBUG and NDEBUG variants use existing real Ker/LKL callbacks without lifecycle mocks or new runtime changes. The iteration count is a host pthread property, not a new protocol or FreeBSD ABI guarantee. Additional Ker TLS failure-path coverage injects pthread_key_create EAGAIN/ENOMEM and pthread_setspecific ENOMEM only in the calling test thread. Failed creation must preserve errno, free storage and permit real key allocation/deletion; failed set must preserve empty or populated slots and allow subsequent real replacement and clearing. Before any threads exist, an injected pthread_key_delete EINVAL must abort through the void callback rather than silently free a still-registered key. Successful operations always use real pthreads; no invalid key is passed to the host API. These are adapter fault-injection tests, not natural host-exhaustion qualification or additional upstream source-case migration. Ker completion adapters preserve pthread_join errors as -1 with errno and abort on an unreportable pthread_detach failure. Per-test-thread wrappers inject EDEADLK/EINVAL/ESRCH without consuming a real joinable thread; each subsequent real join must succeed and observe callback completion. Before any parent host threads, forked child processes validate real self-detach via pthread attributes and injected EINVAL via SIGABRT. No join on detached threads, cancellation or concurrent detached-worker reclamation is claimed. Default, DEBUG and NDEBUG execute the same checks, with original Linux lifecycle and real TCP/UDP regression coverage. Source-case classifications remain unchanged. The Ker thread_stack callback now queries actual pthread stack attributes and publishes the optional size only after a successful range query and attribute cleanup. Errors return NULL with pthread errno and preserve the caller size output; initialized attributes are destroyed even when the range query fails. Default/DEBUG/NDEBUG tests compare callback base/size with an independent real pthread query and require a local variable to lie inside the returned main/child stack range, including a NULL size pointer. Per-test-thread EAGAIN/EINVAL/EIO injections cover attribute lookup, range lookup and post-release cleanup failure, tracking live attributes and requiring real recovery after each failure in both main and child threads. The pinned production kernel is not KASAN-enabled: this qualifies the installed host callback, not KASAN stack unpoisoning or custom/alternate signal stacks. Source-case classifications remain unchanged.

native-fstack-host-runtime.adaptation: Seven pinned F-Stack host-interface scenarios adapted to the actual lkl_host_ops used by Ker: writable allocation and NULL free; nondecreasing monotonic nanoseconds with delayed advancement; anonymous read/write, write-only and read-only mappings with release. LKL mmap takes an exact unused address rather than the ff_mmap(NULL, ...) allocation interface. A Ker-only host callback preserves occupied mappings on failure, without modifying imported LKL. The test checks exact bytes, zero initialization, collision preservation, unmap via mincore, read-only write rejection in a pre-kernel child with core dumps disabled, and page allocator alignment/release. It then boots and halts the real pinned Linux kernel with counted forwarding callbacks to prove kernel memory/time use. The pinned non-MMU kernel uses page_alloc; fixed-address mmap is tested directly through the installed callback table, not claimed as exercised by kernel boot. Shared/file-backed mappings, calloc/realloc, realtime and random interfaces are not covered. Ker page callbacks now use real anonymous read/write mmap and explicitly abort if the void page_free callback cannot unmap its allocation. Exact-address fallback cleanup releases only the returned mapping and reports EEXIST; cleanup failure also aborts. Added default-host DEBUG/NDEBUG tests inject mmap ENOMEM/EAGAIN, validate errno and subsequent real two-page allocation/alignment/zero-fill/write/release, verify real zero-size EINVAL and MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE collision behavior, and simulate an older host returning another real mapping to check cleanup and occupied-byte preservation. Independent pre-thread children inject munmap EINVAL for page_free and fallback cleanup and require SIGABRT. Original Linux boot and TCP/UDP regression use the installed adapters without faults. These extend the same mapping scenarios, not the source-case count; no hugepage, MMU-enabled-kernel, shared/file-backed or concurrent address-reservation claim.

native-fstack-pcap.adaptation: Nine pinned F-Stack PCAP scenarios adapted to the real Ker DPDK packet-I/O capture implementation. Actual EAL mempool mbufs and a two-segment chain are borrowed without ownership changes; native-endian PCAP 2.4 headers, Ethernet linktype, microsecond/nanosecond timestamps, captured/original lengths and exact bytes are independently decoded. Tests cover NULL directory fallback, enable/file creation, disabled writer, nonexistent-path failure, ten-slot wrap with exact retained records, under-limit append, mid-segment snaplen truncation, malformed-chain rejection, rotation-open and buffered-close errors, and zero outstanding buffers. Original Linux TCP active/passive opens and DPDK traffic plus zero outstanding buffers rule out host fallback. CONFIG_IPV6 enables upstream code without protocol source changes. Separate native-dualstack-drain boots the real kernel, fills IPv4 and IPv6 send queues to EAGAIN, requires immediate ETIMEDOUT, consumes/validates every byte and requires drain recovery; the adapter now checks both procfs tables. native-fstack-tcp-linger.adaptation: Ker-specific Linux TCP SO_LINGER/last-reference-close extension of pinned host shutdown and dup bridge scenarios, not an upstream F-Stack test or equivalence claim. Six data connections cover both closer directions and three modes: enable abortive linger then disable it through dup for graceful EOF; leave zero linger enabled and consume reset through recv; consume reset through SO_ERROR instead. Shared queried option values are checked. Closing the original descriptor must leave the alias usable: after a TCP control barrier, the peer observes no poll/epoll readiness for 100 ms and EAGAIN, then receives an exact 17-byte payload through the remaining alias. The final alias closes only after payload consumption acknowledgment. Terminal poll/epoll readiness includes RDHUP/full 64-bit tags and reset ERR/HUP; reset is observed exactly once by the selected consumer, cleared on both aliases, and subsequent reads return EOF. Native instances require seven matching original-Linux TCP opens, DPDK TX/RX and zero outstanding buffers. No runtime/protocol changes, positive linger deadlines, unread-data close, process exit, concurrent close/read or cross-process descriptor transfer coverage is introduced.

native-fstack-udp-receive-truncation.adaptation: Ker-specific consuming UDP receive-truncation extension of the pinned UDP/epoll example, not an upstream F-Stack test or equivalence claim. Datagram lengths 0, 1, 33 and 257 are received into seven-byte capacity. recvfrom without MSG_TRUNC returns copied length; two-iovec recvmsg (3+4 bytes) does likewise and reports output MSG_TRUNC exactly for oversized datagrams without MSG_CTRUNC. Two-entry recvmmsg with input MSG_TRUNC|MSG_DONTWAIT must instead return full per-entry msg_len while copying only the fitting prefix and reporting each truncation flag. One or two returned entries are accepted and actual counts advance the batch; zero-length datagrams still occupy entries. Every copy checks deterministic prefix and untouched 0xa5 canaries, source tuple, full 64-bit epoll tag and FIONREAD full queue-head size before receiving. The peer waits for the next request before the next round, so EAGAIN, zero FIONREAD and no epoll readiness prove truncated suffixes were consumed rather than retained as new datagrams. Final request/ack confirms completion without fixed sleeps. Native client requires UDP OutDatagrams/InDatagrams at least 13/17 and server 17/13, zero UDP input/no-port errors, DPDK TX/RX and zero outstanding buffers. No protocol/runtime changes, recvmmsg timeout/MSG_WAITFORONE, invalid-pointer recovery or network-loss coverage is introduced.

native-fstack-udp-timeouts.adaptation: Ker-specific Linux UDP receive-timeout extension of the pinned UDP example, not an upstream F-Stack test or API equivalence claim. Explicitly bound connected blocking UDP endpoints each test recvfrom, two-iovec recvmsg and one-entry recvmmsg with a NULL timeout pointer. SO_RCVTIMEO=200 ms set through dup is queried from both aliases with kernel rounding allowed. A TCP control channel withholds data until the empty receive has returned EAGAIN; monotonic elapsed time must be at least 100 ms and below four seconds, destination canaries remain untouched, SO_ERROR stays zero and file flags stay blocking. Clearing the socket timeout through the original fd is visible through dup. Each API then recovers on the same socket with a zero-, 17- or 33-byte datagram, verified source tuple, exact payload and canaries; queues end at EAGAIN. Native instances require three original-Linux UDP input/output datagrams each, one matching TCP control open, DPDK TX/RX, zero UDP errors and zero outstanding buffers. No runtime/protocol changes, recvmmsg timeout-pointer semantics, signal interruption, send-buffer pressure, concurrent readers or IPv6 coverage is introduced.

native-fstack-tcp-fd-modes.adaptation: Ker-specific independent-peer fd-mode extension of pinned host nonblocking/dup/message bridge scenarios, not an upstream F-Stack test or equivalence claim. Host-reference and native client/server modes use independent Linux peers over DPDK net_tap/veth with separate control/data connections. Each endpoint receives in turn. Before the sender is released, MSG_DONTWAIT on a blocking socket returns EAGAIN without changing F_GETFL; FIONBIO=1 through dup makes both descriptors nonblocking and ordinary read/recvmsg return EAGAIN; F_SETFL through the original clears shared O_NONBLOCK, another MSG_DONTWAIT leaves it clear, and F_SETFL through the alias enables it again. Poll/epoll with full 64-bit tag drive the first exact payload; FIONBIO=0 through the original restores blocking on both descriptors before a two-iovec MSG_WAITALL receives the exact 17-byte tail and both descriptors observe EOF. No-argument FIOCLEX/FIONCLEX plus F_SETFD separately verify that FD_CLOEXEC is descriptor-local, initially set on the original but absent on dup, and remains independent through mode changes and I/O. Native instances require two matching original-Linux TCP opens, DPDK TX/RX and zero outstanding buffers. No protocol/runtime changes, exec-inheritance support claim, concurrent F_SETFL, mode changes during blocked syscalls or general no-argument ioctl coverage is introduced.

native-fstack-socket-contracts.adaptation: Six Ker-specific public POSIX socket-contract extensions of pinned host bridge name/nonblocking/dup scenarios. native-fstack-readiness.adaptation: Ker-specific poll/select readiness extensions of the pinned FF_KERNEL_COEXIST host readiness and nonblocking bridge scenarios. flow-owner-receive.adaptation: Ker-specific owner receive adapter inspired by the pinned segmented TX scenario. A bounded owner-local packet ring queues chains after flow handoff; worker service polling reuses the Ethernet copy/classify receive path. Destination allocation failure retains one pending chain for FIFO retry; queue overflow explicitly consumes and drops the newest chain. Tests cover allocation recovery during RX pressure, lifecycle pins, cancellation and initialization rollback. This is not upstream F-Stack flow coverage, end-to-end lossless backpressure, NIC/RSS, sockets or TCP state.

neighbor-resolved-output.adaptation: Ker-specific native Linux resolved-neighbor output extension, motivated by the pinned packet-send scenario. The neighbor-timer test sends configured IPv4 frames through unchanged neigh_resolve_output and native event-send inline bodies into the bounded TX exporter. It checks current neighbor MAC header rebuilding, supported NUD states and native timer transitions, TX ownership and retries, and admission failures. Source provenance for the three Linux bodies is verified separately by neighbor-output-import. No upstream F-Stack neighbor test, unknown-neighbor resolution, routing, sockets or NIC transmission is claimed.

neighbor-known-peer-resolution.adaptation: Ker-specific native Linux neighbor re-resolution extension: previously monitored known peer enters INCOMPLETE, queues bounded skb ownership, solicits through explicit ARP callbacks, and flushes via unchanged neighbor update after accepted feedback. Exercises queue pressure, timeout and cancellation. The F-Stack source case motivates packet output only; it is not an upstream neighbor-resolution test and does not establish unknown-peer discovery, routing, sockets or NIC transmission.

neighbor-discovery.adaptation: Ker-specific first-contact neighbor discovery extension: explicitly create a bounded NUD_NONE peer without a supplied MAC, drive native resolution with outbound packets, and consume valid worker ARP feedback to flush queued data. Tests initialization rollback and owned-entry lifecycle. The F-Stack source motivates packet output, not neighbor discovery; full Linux neighbor creation, routing, general ARP learning, sockets and NIC transmission remain outside this slice.

arp-responder.adaptation: Ker-specific responder and two-peer discovery integration extension: the production responder builds a local ARP reply with the native constructor, actual application rings/worker RX deliver it to the discovery peer, and native neighbor output releases queued UDP for transport validation. Tests bounded failures, reply selection and ownership. These upstream cases motivate packet output/segmentation, not an F-Stack ARP responder; full arp_process, general learning, routing and NIC transmission are not claimed.

icmp-echo-service.adaptation: Ker-specific first-contact echo-service integration extension. Two independent skb pools and real SP/SC rings carry a validated echo request, native neighbor resolution emits an ARP probe through the existing responder and scoped feedback path, and the returned echo reply is checked by the peer transport callback. This is not the F-Stack socket, ping, full ICMP input/reply path, routing, or NIC delivery.

icmpv4-service.adaptation: Ker-specific ICMPv4 control extension: generic error events, bounded safe error emission, timestamp and opt-in extended echo, token-bucket limits and independent peer pools with actual RX/TX rings. The source cases motivate packet delivery only; no upstream ICMP suite, sockets, routing, IPv4 reassembly, IPv6 or NIC delivery is claimed. The same real-ring fixture also exercises an opt-in bounded Ker UDP endpoint table: validated local datagrams reach bound callbacks, while lookup misses automatically generate ICMP port-unreachable through the existing neighbor output. This is not native Linux socket lookup or a F-Stack UDP ingress test. Explicit immutable unavailable-protocol declarations additionally drive automatic ICMP protocol-unreachable for validated local IPv4 ingress, with competing-handler suppression. This is a Ker policy adapter, not Linux inet_protos/raw socket/XFRM integration. Connected endpoint regressions extend the Ker-specific UDP adapter with generation-scoped handles and exact peer filtering; these are not upstream F-Stack socket tests.

flow-icmpv4.adaptation: Ker-specific UDP control-flow steering extension: ICMPv4 errors quote an outbound UDP tuple which must resolve to the same flow owner as its response. Real segmented DPDK chains cover every header split, truncated quotes, declared lengths, Ethernet padding, unsupported options/fragments/protocols, wrong quoted local address and ingress-only direction. Steering does not authenticate ICMP or validate checksums; those remain the owner receiver and sent-evidence tracker responsibilities. This is not a F-Stack upstream ICMP test, NIC/RSS, TCP or IPv6 control-plane implementation.

ethdev-rx.adaptation: Ker-specific borrowed ethdev RX extension around the existing worker receive path. A real pinned DPDK net_ring PMD injects Ethernet frames and segmented mbuf chains; the test checks one-packet worker budgets, FIFO classification/dispatch, pool-pressure retry, cancellation, and RX binding exclusion. Opt-in immutable shared-reference profiles test direct shared segments, actual rte_pktmbuf_clone chains, and attached external-buffer chains, including caller/sibling lifetime, extbuf callbacks and allocation retry. The upstream case only motivates one worker-loop iteration and stop; pinned free/fanout scenarios do not test indirect-clone or external-buffer RX. No NIC, RSS, socket, or full-stack behavior is claimed.

ethdev-rebind.adaptation: Ker-specific borrowed ethdev RX lifecycle extension. A real started net_ring port keeps a queued successor behind a pending frame across adapter/device/runtime teardown; a fresh callback generation rebinds the same queue and consumes it first. The test covers pending-packet cleanup exclusion, exact cancellation, invalid rebind rollback, FIFO delivery and pool reclamation. The upstream registration roundtrip motivates lifecycle testing only; PMD queues are caller-owned and are not implicitly flushed, and this does not implement full F-Stack device registration.

ethdev-duplex.adaptation: Ker-specific composition test: two actual pinned DPDK net_ring ethdev ports cross-connect bounded TX/RX queues; each Ker worker polls the existing ethdev TX and RX adapters through its shared worker callback argument. Distinct source/destination pools carry multisegment software-checksummed TCP and UDP packets through the original Ethernet classifier and transport views. Independent checksum verification, FIFO, full-ring retry, destination-pool pressure retention, callback drop, ownership, and pool reclamation are checked. The F-Stack cases motivate the worker/send/checksum boundaries only; this is not an F-Stack stack, hardware-offload, NIC, or application-protocol test.

ethdev-multiqueue.adaptation: Ker-specific multi-EAL ethdev queue-isolation extension motivated by the upstream SP/SC drain scenario. Two owner workers on distinct EAL lcores use independent bounded net_ring ethdev queues, contexts, pools, and existing TX/RX adapters. The test checks real worker dispatch, queue-0 backpressure while queue 1 progresses, recovery, checksum/payload identity, and wrong-owner rejection. It does not test upstream ring reload, RSS, multiprocess operation, physical NICs, or full F-Stack.

ethdev-rx-metadata.adaptation: Ker-specific RX trust-boundary extension: a real net_ring PMD feeds TCP/UDP frames through ethdev RX, the worker, the original Ethernet classifier and existing transport packet views. GOOD/BAD/UNKNOWN checksum hints never bypass software wire validation; NONE and transformed metadata are rejected. The pinned F-Stack cases are TX checksum-offload scenarios and do not cover this RX path or hardware/NIC checksum behavior.

ethdev-external-lifetime.adaptation: Ker-specific final-reference RX lifetime extension motivated by the upstream basic mbuf release case. A real net_ring ethdev feeds mixed external/direct/external chains into the existing copy/classify/dispatch adapter. No parent or sibling reference is retained. Actual DPDK external-buffer callbacks poison and quarantine released storage; retained owned skbs are checked before and after physical source deallocation. Repeated allocation failure, partial-budget FIFO recovery, cancellation transfer, transformed-metadata drop, exact callback counts, PMD receive counts and full source/destination pool reclamation are verified. The pinned upstream case only frees one basic mbuf and does not test external-buffer RX, deferred skb ownership, NICs, hardware offload or protocol behavior.

ethdev-rx-capacity.adaptation: Ker-specific RX linear-copy capacity extension motivated by the pinned multisegment TX case. Real net_ring RX carries small source-pool segments into an independently sized destination pool. Capacity-minus-one, exact capacity and capacity-plus-one are checked with three headrooms and a non-cache-line-aligned destination room size. With the destination pool exhausted, permanently oversized frames are consumed as ENOSPC drops before a fitting successor becomes ENOMEM pending; releasing one backing permits exact FIFO recovery. Direct allocation error precedence, byte preservation, Linux shared-info reservation, PMD packet counts and both pool baselines are verified. Payloads are opaque: no IPv4/TCP/UDP protocol processing, jumbo MTU negotiation, NIC, nonlinear skb or F-Stack RX support is claimed.

ethdev-rx-fanout.adaptation: Ker-specific Linux packet_type fanout and ownership extension. Real net_ring RX supplies segmented opaque Ethernet frames through the actual worker, original Ethernet classification and imported Linux ptype delivery. Global-before-device ordering, per-callback descriptor references, final-handler status, explicit invalid-status reporting, no-handler drop, retained skb lifetime, cloned backing, COW ENOMEM rollback/recovery, independent header/payload mutation, both release orders and full pool reclamation are checked. The pinned F-Stack cases motivate worker iteration and basic ownership only; they do not test Linux ptype fanout or COW. No F-Stack RX, NIC, IP/transport processing or application-protocol behavior is claimed.

native-fstack-epoll.adaptation: Ten public POSIX scenarios use real loopback TCP connections, first on the host Linux baseline and then through libker-posix with the complete pinned Linux kernel. Covers create/invalid values, ADD/MOD/DEL and full 64-bit event data, level readiness while partially unread, ET drain/new data, ONESHOT explicit rearm, write-only readiness, buffered EOF with reverse-direction data, and abortive-close ERR/HUP with SO_ERROR. Kernel open counters and empty outstanding DPDK allocation counts are required. The same CTest also retains independent host TCP/DPDK interop checks. No ff implementation, FreeBSD stack, kqueue translation, synthetic events or cmocka stubs are copied. Linux rejects epoll_create(0), unlike the upstream stub; half-close uses EPOLLRDHUP instead of assuming EV_EOF translates to EPOLLHUP. Arbitrary invalid-pointer and synthetic unknown-kqueue-filter cases are not claimed. Full-suite inventory adds NULL ADD/MOD event recovery: Linux EFAULT replaces the upstream wrapper EINVAL; Ker must reject NULL before the LKL user-copy path dereferences it. DEL with NULL remains valid. Existing write-only, zero-maxevents and empty-FIN scenarios cover the corresponding additional upstream registrations. Unknown FreeBSD filter translation has no Linux equivalent and remains separately classified. NULL wait-buffer adaptation covers epoll_wait, epoll_pwait and epoll_pwait2: invalid maxevents yields EINVAL; empty zero-time waits return zero; ready native ET/ONESHOT events fault with EFAULT and remain deliverable to a valid buffer. A host pipe in mixed-domain epoll also retains ONESHOT readiness after EFAULT. F-Stack rejects NULL unconditionally with EINVAL; Linux only faults when copying an event. The adapter probes native epoll readiness rather than passing NULL into shared-address-space user copies. No arbitrary inaccessible-pointer or concurrent-consumer recovery is claimed.

native-fstack-message-io.adaptation: Six public POSIX behavioral scenarios run on host Linux and the complete imported Linux TCP stack, comparing successful scenario output and requiring at least six native active/passive opens plus zero outstanding DPDK buffers. Adapts the FF_KERNEL_COEXIST host bridge tests for sendmsg/recvmsg, address lookup, half-close, readv/writev, FIONBIO, dup and dup2. Unlike the upstream host-only bridge cases, the adapted AF_INET pairs must use native TCP under ker-run; the AF_UNIX vector roundtrip remains explicit host passthrough. Ker-specific extensions cover zero-length iovecs, stream short reads without MSG_TRUNC, MSG_PEEK/DONTWAIT, FIONREAD, shared O_NONBLOCK and independent descriptor CLOEXEC, and fixed-fd host/native replacement with post-replacement byte checks. No ff implementation, mock or FreeBSD protocol code is copied. Loopback scenarios do not exercise DPDK traffic; the same CTest separately runs existing independent-host-peer active/passive TCP interop and verifies DPDK counters. No new protocol implementation or zero-copy, ancillary-data, IPv6, fork, or io_uring support is claimed.

native-fstack-stream-io.adaptation: Ker-specific independent-peer extension: public POSIX TCP programs run vector (writev/readv), message (sendmsg/recvmsg), and batched-message (sendmmsg/recvmmsg) modes against an independent host Linux endpoint over DPDK net_tap/veth. Each mode runs with Ker as client and as server, for six role/API combinations. Every direction validates 256 KiB + 13 bytes using direction-specific patterns, nonblocking progress/retry handling, zero-length vector entries where applicable, half-close and exact EOF. Batched TCP I/O is treated as a byte stream rather than preserving message boundaries. Small send buffers exercise backpressure; observed partial/retry counts are logged without imposing scheduler-dependent counts as performance requirements. Each native instance must show TX/RX, the matching native active/passive open, and zero outstanding packet buffers; both peer programs must report successful byte verification. Upstream covers small host-only bridge transfers, not this native TCP/DPDK or batched-message behavior. No ff implementation, FreeBSD stack, mock, new protocol path, zero-copy, ancillary-data, or io_uring support is added.

native-fstack-udp-interop.adaptation: Ker-specific native UDP socket extension motivated by pinned UDP TX-checksum coverage and the public UDP/epoll example. The upstream checksum case tests TX offload metadata, not UDP socket semantics; the example is not an upstream automated test and ignores empty datagrams, unlike this validation. Three modes (sendto/recvfrom, sendmsg/recvmsg, sendmmsg/recvmmsg) run with Ker as both client and server against independent host Linux peers over DPDK net_tap/veth. Each direction verifies four distinct datagrams of lengths 0, 1, 33 and 257; checks peer tuples, epoll readiness, connected UDP in message mode, FIONREAD, MSG_PEEK/MSG_TRUNC, and empty-queue EAGAIN without interpreting zero payload as EOF. Every native instance requires positive DPDK TX/RX, at least four original-Linux UDP InDatagrams/OutDatagrams, zero UDP input/no-port errors and zero outstanding buffers. Protocol behavior is the complete imported Linux UDP implementation, not the basic Ker packet constructors/views. The change adds private native diagnostics fields; it does not change protocol sources, the TCP capability declaration, DNS, IPv6, multicast, fragmentation or error-queue coverage.

native-fstack-udp-errors.adaptation: Ker-specific Linux error-queue extension of the pinned UDP socket/epoll example; IP_RECVERR is not claimed as an upstream F-Stack test or API. The same POSIX assertions run first on host Linux and then on the complete imported Linux kernel with connected and unconnected UDP. An independent host kernel generates real ICMP port-unreachable for an unused port in an isolated namespace. Tests require unsolicited EPOLLERR, SO_ERROR ECONNREFUSED, persistent queue readiness after SO_ERROR is read, quoted payload and destination, sock_extended_err errno/origin/type/code and offender address, empty-queue EAGAIN, cleared error readiness, and verified echo recovery on the same socket. Native runs require original-Linux UDP counters, DPDK TX/RX and zero outstanding buffers. No synthetic ICMP, protocol implementation, ff implementation, mock, kernel source change, general ancillary-data, IPv6 or io_uring support is introduced.

native-fstack-udp-ancillary.adaptation: Ker-specific Linux ancillary-data extension of the pinned UDP socket/epoll example, not an upstream F-Stack ancillary test. The same C program runs on host Linux and with the complete imported Linux kernel as client and wildcard-bound server against independent host peers over DPDK. Three datagrams per direction verify payload and source tuple, IP_PKTINFO destination/local address and interface identity, per-message source/interface selection, and SO_TIMESTAMPNS receive timestamps within the host realtime interval (one-second boundary tolerance). A one-byte control buffer must report MSG_CTRUNC without payload truncation; the following datagram must again deliver both complete control messages. Native UDP counters, DPDK TX/RX and zero outstanding buffers are required. The timestamp assertion exposed the LKL POSIX monotonic persistent-clock seed; Ker initializes only the private kernel realtime clock from host CLOCK_REALTIME after boot, preserving upstream clocksource and protocol code. No ff implementation, mock, hardware timestamps, continuous host clock synchronization, general ancillary support or new protocol implementation is claimed.

native-fstack-udp-mtu.adaptation: Ker-specific IPv4 MTU and fragmentation extension of the pinned UDP/epoll example, not an upstream F-Stack MTU test. Host-reference and imported-Linux client/server runs verify IP_MTU=1500; IP_PMTUDISC_DO rejects 1473-byte payloads with EMSGSIZE, unsolicited EPOLLERR and a local IP_RECVERR entry reporting MTU 1500, original destination and AF_UNSPEC offender. A 1472-byte datagram succeeds under DO. Switching to DONT permits 1473, 4096 and 65507-byte datagrams with exact byte/tuple verification in both directions. A 65508-byte send is rejected and its local error queue is drained before another successful datagram on the same socket. Private diagnostics read original-Linux Ip FragOKs/FragCreates/ReasmOKs/ReasmFails; each native instance must fragment and reassemble three datagrams, create at least 50 fragments, show DPDK TX/RX, verify five UDP datagrams each direction and reclaim all packet buffers. The isolated host-reference loopback MTU is set to 1500 only for this test. No protocol source changes, synthetic fragments, remote-router PMTU discovery, fragment loss/reordering, IPv6, offload or hardware NIC coverage is claimed.

native-fstack-udp-multicast.adaptation: Ker-specific IPv4 multicast extension of the pinned UDP/epoll example, not an upstream F-Stack multicast test. One host-reference and native sender/receiver runs use public POSIX sockets over DPDK net_tap/veth with group 239.255.42.17. Two SO_REUSEADDR receivers bound to one port must both receive the first datagram; after one leaves and closes, the other leaves, checks duplicate-leave EADDRNOTAVAIL, rejoins, and receives the next datagram. A unicast acknowledgement is sent only after rejoin to avoid a sender race. Checks duplicate-join EADDRINUSE, IP_MULTICAST_ALL=0, IP_MULTICAST_IF, TTL=7, loop option, source tuples, IP_PKTINFO group/local address and positive interface, IP_RECVTTL, payload and readiness. Native sender requires two UDP inputs/outputs; native receiver requires three inputs and two outputs, plus DPDK TX/RX, no UDP errors and zero outstanding buffers. The test exposed missing PMD multicast admission; an explicit ker-run/worker --all-multicast option now enables and verifies ethdev all-multicast reception, leaving membership/protocol filtering to original Linux and failing startup if unavailable. No upstream source modification, protocol substitute, group MAC subscription bridge, drop-interval non-delivery proof, IGMP router interoperability, source-specific multicast, IPv6 or physical NIC coverage is claimed.

native-fstack-tcp-receive-timeouts.adaptation: Ker-specific blocking receive/half-close and duplicated-descriptor extension of the pinned host bridge scenarios, not an upstream F-Stack timeout test. The same public POSIX program runs as a host reference and with the complete imported Linux kernel as client and server over DPDK net_tap/veth. Before READY, a blocking listener must time out accept with EAGAIN; its accepted socket inherits SO_RCVTIMEO and remains blocking. The client checks recv/recvmsg/readv empty-queue EAGAIN after a configured 120ms timeout, invalid microseconds EDOM without changing the prior option, shared timeout state through dup, MSG_WAITALL returning five existing bytes when no suffix arrives before timeout, a following empty-read timeout, disabling timeout through the alias, and partial WAITALL completion at EOF with successful reverse-direction acknowledgement. Explicit application handshakes suppress peer data until requested, and poll establishes that the first five bytes are queued before partial-WAITALL timing. Timing checks allow tick/scheduler variation (50ms to 5s) and are not a precision/performance claim. Native client exercises the receive cases; native server exercises listener timeout/inheritance and peer progress. Each native instance requires matching original-Linux TCP open counts, DPDK TX/RX and no outstanding packet buffers. No protocol changes, mocks, signal interruption/cancellation, send timeout, TCP connect-timeout or general time64 ABI support is added.

native-fstack-tcp-send-timeouts.adaptation: Ker-specific blocking send/backpressure extension, not an upstream F-Stack timeout test. Host-reference and native client/server runs use a dedicated TCP control connection plus a small-buffer TCP data connection over DPDK net_tap/veth. Each endpoint takes a turn sending 512 KiB + 13 direction-specific bytes while its peer withholds application reads until a control marker. SO_SNDTIMEO=120ms must yield positive partial send progress, then no-progress EAGAIN via send, writev and sendmsg; all positive return lengths advance the source offset. Invalid microseconds return EDOM without replacing the prior value. Clearing the timeout through dup must affect the original fd. After an explicit resume marker, the peer enlarges its receive buffer, verifies the entire byte stream, acknowledges completion on the control connection, and the roles reverse. Both directions end at exact EOF without extra bytes. Elapsed checks allow 50ms..5s and option tick rounding, not precise timing. Each native instance requires two matching original-Linux TCP opens, DPDK TX/RX and zero outstanding buffers. No protocol or runtime adapter changes, mocks, host signal interruption/cancellation, connect-timeout or general time64 ABI support is introduced.

native-fstack-tcp-connect-lifecycle.adaptation: Ker-specific Linux TCP connect/error and epoll lifetime extension of the pinned host bridge scenarios, not an upstream F-Stack AF_UNSPEC reconnect test. Host-reference and native client/server runs use independent Linux peers over DPDK net_tap/veth. One nonblocking client socket plus its dup alias receives ECONNREFUSED from an unused port; poll/epoll report error readiness, reading SO_ERROR through the alias clears it for the original fd, and error readiness clears without assuming HUP/writable readiness disappears. AF_UNSPEC resets the socket; it connects to the first listener, verifies peer tuples and echo, then AF_UNSPEC aborts that live connection (the server must observe ECONNRESET). Any local reset error is cleared, and the same socket reconnects to a different listener port without replacing the epoll registration. Closing the originally registered fd must retain readiness and I/O through the live alias; the final exchange, half-close and EOF succeed with the full 64-bit event tag intact. Native client requires three active opens; native server requires two passive opens, plus positive DPDK TX/RX, both endpoint PASS results and zero outstanding buffers. Original Linux owns refusal, reset and reconnect semantics. No protocol/adapter changes, mocks, portable AF_UNSPEC guarantee, concurrent close stress, host signal interruption or io_uring coverage is introduced.

native-fstack-tcp-defer-accept.adaptation: Ker-specific Linux TCP_DEFER_ACCEPT extension motivated by pinned host socket/readiness bridge scenarios, not an upstream F-Stack deferred-accept test or support claim. Host reference and native client/server modes use independent Linux peers over DPDK net_tap/veth. A separate control connection coordinates two sequential data connections on the same nonblocking listener. With deferred accept enabled (31 seconds, permitting kernel rounding), completed client connect with checked peer tuple and SO_ERROR must not make the listener readable during a 100ms poll, an immediate epoll wait, or nonblocking accept (EAGAIN). Payload is withheld until an explicit control marker, then poll/epoll and accept must succeed. Clearing the option on that listener permits the second handshake to trigger readiness and accept before payload is sent. Both phases verify exact echo, half-close/EOF, drained listener readiness and a full 64-bit epoll tag. Each native instance requires at least three matching original-Linux TCP opens, positive DPDK TX/RX and zero outstanding buffers. No original protocol/runtime changes, mocks, deferred timer expiry, TCP Fast Open, host signal interruption or io_uring coverage is introduced.

native-fstack-tcp-reuseport.adaptation: Ker-specific Linux SO_REUSEPORT extension motivated by pinned host socket/readiness bridge scenarios, not an upstream F-Stack reuseport test or equivalence claim. Host-reference and native client/server modes use independent Linux peers over DPDK net_tap/veth. Two nonblocking listeners enable and query SO_REUSEPORT before sharing an address/port; a third socket with SO_REUSEADDR alone must fail bind with EADDRINUSE. A separate control connection coordinates eight initial data connections and four later connections. Poll/epoll drive accepts; unique tokens verify every connection exactly once without requiring equal hash distribution or both listeners to receive initial connections. The test retains the token=1 accepted connection, closes precisely the listener that accepted it, and requires continued echo and half-close/EOF on the accepted connection. The remaining listener must accept all four later connections, with exact echo, EOF, full 64-bit epoll tags and cleared readiness after the queue drains. Each native instance requires thirteen matching original-Linux TCP opens, DPDK TX/RX and zero outstanding buffers. No protocol/runtime changes, mocks, pending-connection migration, cross-process workers, UID isolation, BPF selection or io_uring coverage is introduced.

native-fstack-tcp-urgent.adaptation: Ker-specific Linux urgent-data extension motivated by pinned host socket/readiness bridge scenarios, not an upstream F-Stack urgent-data test or equivalence claim. The existing Ker loopback OOB case is extended to independent host Linux peers over DPDK net_tap/veth, with host-reference and native client/server runs. Two data connections disable/enable SO_OOBINLINE and exercise both directions. A separate control connection orders receiver option setup and EPOLLPRI registration, six ordinary prefix bytes, one MSG_OOB byte, and five ordinary suffix bytes, without fixed sleeps. Poll/epoll must report priority readiness with full 64-bit tags. SIOCATMARK via public ioctl changes from false before prefix consumption to true at the urgent boundary; POSIX sockatmark must match each ioctl result. The new sockatmark adapter/export reuses existing ioctl dispatch because libc internal ioctl bypasses native fd routing. Invalid fd EBADF, host pipe ENOTTY and host socket reference behavior are checked. Out-of-line mode peeks then consumes MSG_OOB without duplicating the urgent byte in the ordinary stream; inline mode rejects MSG_OOB with EINVAL and consumes the urgent byte through ordinary recv. Exact suffix and half-close/EOF must clear urgent mark and PRI while allowing persistent EOF/HUP readiness. Native instances require three matching original-Linux TCP opens, DPDK TX/RX and zero outstanding buffers. No original protocol changes, SIGURG/async ownership, overwriting multiple outstanding urgent pointers or io_uring coverage is introduced.

native-fstack-tcp-receive-queue.adaptation: Ker-specific Linux TCP receive-queue extension of pinned host message/vector/dup bridge scenarios, not an upstream F-Stack test or equivalence claim. Host-reference and native client/server modes use independent Linux peers over DPDK net_tap/veth. Each direction sends 16 KiB + 37 deterministic bytes and half-closes; a separate control connection and SO_RCVLOWAT coordinate a complete queued payload without fixed sleeps, then restore the low-water mark to one. Two-iovec recvmsg(MSG_PEEK|MSG_WAITALL) through dup and a 6001-byte peek through the original fd verify bytes without changing FIONREAD on either alias. Linux TCP recv(MSG_TRUNC) consumes 257 bytes without modifying destination canaries; recvmsg(MSG_PEEK|MSG_TRUNC) reports 513 bytes without copying or consuming. Remaining bytes are verified through readv on the alias, with exact original-fd queue counts after each read; both aliases and ordinary peek observe EOF and zero FIONREAD, excluding FIN from payload counts. These Linux TCP flag semantics are distinct from UDP datagram truncation and are not a portable POSIX claim. Each native instance requires two matching original-Linux TCP opens, DPDK TX/RX and zero outstanding buffers. No protocol/runtime changes, concurrent-reader stress, SO_PEEK_OFF, invalid-pointer recovery or io_uring coverage is introduced.

native-fstack-tcp-shutdown-write.adaptation: Ker-specific Linux local SHUT_WR extension of pinned host shutdown/message/vector/dup bridge scenarios, distinct from existing peer-RST validation and not an upstream F-Stack test or equivalence claim. Host-reference and native client/server modes use independent Linux peers over DPDK net_tap/veth. Invalid shutdown how=42 returns EINVAL without breaking later normal sends. SHUT_WR through dup shares send shutdown with the original fd. Repeated shutdown succeeds while the peer keeps its send direction open; once both FINs are ACKed Linux may return ENOTCONN instead. send/sendto/sendmsg/one-entry sendmmsg with MSG_NOSIGNAL must return EPIPE without SIGPIPE; the same APIs without the flag plus write/writev must each return EPIPE with exactly one handled SIGPIPE, six signals per endpoint and unchanged zero SO_ERROR. A separate control connection keeps the peer receive socket open until all probes finish, distinguishing local shutdown from peer-close errors without fixed sleeps. A client that has shut down writes must still receive the full reverse server reply through its alias; the server performs the same error matrix. Both endpoints verify EOF, poll/epoll IN plus RDHUP and full 64-bit tags. Native instances require two matching original-Linux TCP opens, DPDK TX/RX and zero outstanding buffers. No protocol/runtime changes, SHUT_RD, blocked/ignored/default-action SIGPIPE, async signal ownership or partial-success sendmmsg signal behavior is introduced.

native-fstack-udp-broadcast.adaptation: Ker-specific IPv4 subnet broadcast extension of the pinned UDP/epoll example, not an upstream F-Stack broadcast test or API equivalence claim. Host-reference and native client/server runs use independent Linux peers over DPDK net_tap/veth and subnet broadcast 198.18.0.255/24. The wildcard-bound receiver keeps SO_BROADCAST disabled; the sender explicitly binds and verifies its local address. sendto, sendmsg and one-entry sendmmsg must each fail with EACCES while SO_BROADCAST is disabled, then send one 37-byte broadcast request after enabling/querying it. Each unicast reply is followed by disabling/querying the option. A final denied broadcast and successful same-socket unicast exchange verify recovery with the option still disabled. Every datagram validates payload, source tuple, EPOLLIN/full 64-bit tag and IP_PKTINFO destination/local address/positive interface identity. Broadcast and unicast may use different interface indexes in the same-kernel host reference. Native instances require UDP InDatagrams/OutDatagrams at least four each, zero UDP input/no-port errors, DPDK TX/RX and zero outstanding buffers; queues end at EAGAIN. No protocol/runtime/device-mode changes, limited broadcast 255.255.255.255, multi-interface routing, forwarded broadcasts, physical NIC filtering, fragmented broadcast or discovery-protocol support is introduced.

native-fstack-udp-connect-lifecycle.adaptation: Ker-specific Linux UDP connect lifecycle extension of the pinned UDP/epoll example, not an upstream F-Stack test or equivalence claim. Host-reference and native client/server modes use independent Linux peers over DPDK net_tap/veth. One client socket and dup explicitly bind a local address and nonzero port. Connecting through the alias to A sets the original fd peer; default sends reach A. A foreign-source B datagram must produce a real IP_RECVERR ICMP port-unreachable at B, validating quoted token/destination, origin/type/code and offender before A sends its valid reply; the client queue then ends at EAGAIN. Reconnecting the original fd to B changes the alias peer and default destination while preserving the local tuple. Explicit sendto A succeeds without changing the connected peer: an A reply must still be source-filtered and positively confirmed through ICMP, then B sends valid acknowledgment and receives the next default send. AF_UNSPEC through the alias clears getpeername (ENOTCONN), preserves both explicitly bound local tuples, and makes destination-less send fail EDESTADDRREQ without SO_ERROR.
